title: Start in 60 minutes
intro: Start with a small piece of work in a project you control. Use Codex or Cursor; the packs share the same boundaries but use different project paths.
promise: Within the first 35 minutes, aim for one useful, checked result. The rest of the hour is for keeping only the guidance and records you need.

steps.title: Choose a small task and your host
steps.why: Use a project you control and a task whose result you can check.
steps.do: Download the Codex or Cursor pack. Start with a read-only job: explain one failing test, naming the file, likely cause and one way to check it.
steps.proof: A task with a clear finish, and the selected pack unpacked beside the project.

steps.title: Merge guidance and check the boundaries
steps.do: Codex: merge AGENTS.md and .agents/ into the project root. Cursor: merge .cursor/rules/ and .cursor/skills/. Compare conflicts before changing existing files. Keep secrets out of chat; agree the exact scope before consequential actions. Start a new task and ask which guidance and skill paths it can read. Check host permissions separately.
steps.proof: You can distinguish the instructions it read from controls the host actually enforces.

steps.title: Do useful work
steps.why: A result tells you more than a completed setup checklist.
steps.do: Run the small task now. For example: “Read this failing test and its implementation. Explain the likely cause and suggest a focused check. Do not edit files.” Require file references and the limits of the diagnosis.
steps.proof: A useful answer checked against the source, with no unrequested edits.

steps.title: Adapt a skill if the job will recur
steps.why: Keep a procedure only when it helps repeat the work.
steps.do: Codex: edit .agents/skills/example-domain-task/SKILL.md. Cursor: edit .cursor/skills/example-domain-task/SKILL.md. Rename it for your recurring job, with matching triggers and proof of done. Try that job with the skill.
steps.proof: The skill describes your job and its result can be checked. Skip it for a one-off task.

steps.title: Record a pattern only if there is a lesson
steps.why: An example row is not your own approval.
steps.do: Read patterns/WORKING-PATTERNS.md. Codex examples include one-writer-per-tree and one-bounded-diagnostic-pass; Cursor examples include lean-tool-sessions and trash-instead-of-hard-delete. Keep or adapt one only if it matches an observed problem. A signed-off row records editorial agreement, not permission to execute an action.
steps.proof: Any retained pattern names a real problem; otherwise leave it proposed.

steps.title: Set dates if you want to track tenure
steps.why: Preserve history rather than making the setup look older.
steps.do: Both packs have clocks.json: set harness.start to today. The Codex pack also has codex.start: use the first day you used Codex on real project work, or leave it unset if unknown. Do not add a Codex date to the Cursor stub.
steps.proof: Any dates you keep are honest; clocks are optional records.

steps.title: Finish with the result
steps.why: Short tasks can finish in chat.
steps.do: Report what you found or changed, how you checked it and anything unresolved. If something failed, diagnose the mechanism before adding a rule: a smaller task, clearer instruction or runtime restriction may help. Review later only when requested or an observed problem warrants it.
steps.proof: One checked result. No routine reflection note or calendar appointment required.

done.title: Done when
checks: Existing project instructions preserved and selected host paths checked
Secrets boundary understood; human decisions and host enforcement kept separate
One useful task completed with evidence and limits
Any skill, pattern or dates retained serve a real need

next: Read the Playbook or Learning sections when a problem calls for them. The Token Bonfire describes what happened when improving the process became more work than the task.
